raw_response:
I’m old now, so I don’t toss things around much. On my 3 mu, I’ll still do wheat and maize like always. This land has followed this way for many years, and for a small household like ours, it is the safest. Wheat gives us a steady harvest, and maize follows right after, so even if one season is not so good, the other can still help. I only finished one stage of school, so I don’t calculate too fine. I look at what my field did last year, what the neighbors are doing, and how much cash I can spare. Fertilizer is expensive, but if I cut too much and the crop turns yellow, then the loss is bigger. So I’ll use a moderate amount, not the highest, not too little. Since I have well water, I will irrigate wheat a few times because wheat here usually needs it; maize I will watch the rain first and only pump if the field is too dry. I won’t do anything fancy. I’ll use the seed we can buy locally, apply fertilizer in two splits for each crop, spray only if weeds or insects show up badly, and keep tillage simple because after wheat harvest the maize planting window is very short.
